source.title: Human-Annotated Label Noise and Their Impact on ConvNets for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
source.authors: Long Peng; T. Wei; Xue-Hong Chen; Xiao-Bei Chen; Rui Sun; Luo-Ma Wan; Jin Chen; Xiao-Lin Zhu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, though it contains minor OCR/typographical errors.
record.tranche_reason: Tests human-annotated and simulated label noise in remote-sensing scene classifiers, extending label-noise findings to a new dataset and domain. It does not test the specified random-label fitting claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on classifiers trained with real human annotation errors and three simulated noise types. It does not report training error or training time for random labels; V1–V6 are therefore not tested. Results cited from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The uniform-noise experiments test V4's test-performance component in a remote-sensing setting: test accuracy declines as randomly corrupted label fractions increase. They do not establish perfect training fit or degradation over the full zero-to-all corruption range. Human, class-dependent and instance-dependent noise results address different noise structures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that human annotation noise has both class and instance dependence, affects classifier accuracy and error patterns, and is partly tolerated. Its effects generally exceed simulated noise, with case-dependent robustness. The overall-accuracy contrast against class-dependent noise was not statistically significant (p = .084), so greater impact should not be asserted as significant for every simulated-noise comparison.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tuned ImageNet-pretrained ConvNets on human or simulated noisy remote-sensing labels; no random-label memorization procedure. Training used RAdam at learning rate 10-4, batch size 128, cross-entropy, and ReduceLROnPlateau.
record.method_sensitivity: Model architecture and noise type affected accuracy, error-pattern similarity, and robustness; category also affected robustness comparisons in the appendix.

fits_no_version.finding: Human annotation errors significantly reduced test accuracy for all three architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Structured human annotation noise reduces remote-sensing classifier accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Models' test-error patterns were more similar to their corresponding annotators' error patterns than random pairings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human training-label confusion structure transfers to classifier test errors.

fits_no_version.finding: Each percentage-point reduction in human-label accuracy corresponded to 0.56, 0.42 and 0.46 percentage-point reductions in model accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These pretrained classifiers tolerate some structured human annotation noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-dependent and instance-dependent noise reduced accuracy, and robustness comparisons depended on architecture and noise structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifier robustness to structured label noise depends on the noise-generation process and architecture.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
record.problems: Only six of the 21 UCMerced categories were used. The human-label training set had 240 images and the test set 360 images. Models used ImageNet-pretrained weights, so this is not a from-scratch random-label fitting test. Exact OA and correlation values are presented in figures rather than stated in text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports error-pattern similarity comparisons and detailed robustness comparisons among simulated-noise types. These are not expanded into additional rows where the text gives only aggregate comparisons or figure-only values; row coverage prioritizes stated per-model accuracy and human-noise results.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and fitting under unchanged training settings.
Relative training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit, the full zero-to-all corruption sweep, convergence toward chance, and direct evidence of memorizing noise while capturing signal. Reported regressions summarize the sampled noise levels rather than establishing pointwise monotonicity.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout and augmentation on random-label fitting and clean-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket exclusion of V4 overlooks its explicitly named test-error component. Support here is confined to that component and the sampled corruption levels; missing training-fit and endpoint measurements are untested, not evidence against the claim. States of cannot_determine for unlinked rows concern V1–V6, not the validity of the reported unrelated effects.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, training error, chance test error, unchanged architecture and hyperparameters, and comparison with true labels.
Training time and convergence as a function of the fraction of corrupted labels.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
A controlled sweep from zero to all randomly corrupted labels, perfect training fit, and steadily increasing test error.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effect on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Training-time order of learning real-label patterns and memorizing noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: VGG16
rows.operation_detail: Trained on each participant’s human labels for 240 images; evaluated on 360 test images.
rows.measure: Overall accuracy on test set versus ideal model trained with error-free labels.
rows.baseline: OA of ideal model trained with error-free training dataset (value not stated).
rows.value: Significantly lower OA; one-sample t-test t(31) = -7.719, p < .0001.
rows.uncertainty: p < .0001; mean and SD shown in Fig. 7, exact values not stated.
rows.note: Thirty-two participant-specific model copies; paper reports the aggregate test and significance result.
rows.check: Human annotation noise and test accuracy do not measure a specified version.

relationships.condition: Test-performance component; ImageNet-pretrained VGG16, GoogLeNet and ResNet-50 fine-tuned with uniform random label corruption at participant-matched noise rates.
relationships.reason: R10–R12 show lower test accuracy than clean-label controls; R19–R21 report declining test accuracy as corruption increases, described collectively as around 0.5 percentage points or less per additional percentage point of noise.
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy fell below clean-label controls and declined by around 0.5 percentage points or less per additional percentage point of noise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
